key_insight: EventHub replaces costly active-sensor ground truth (e.g., LiDAR) with proxy annotations and synthesized event streams derived from standard color images, enabling training of accurate, generalizable event-based stereo networks without active sensors.
problem_solved: Training event-based stereo networks typically requires expensive or hard-to-acquire ground truth from active sensors; EventHub eliminates that dependency by generating usable training data from ordinary RGB images.
method: Data factory: convert image datasets into training pairs by (a) synthesizing proxy events via novel view synthesis (NVS) or (b) using existing image–event pairs to produce proxy disparity/annotations.
Repurpose state-of-the-art RGB stereo architectures to work with event-derived inputs and proxy labels, enabling direct training of event-based stereo models.
Train and validate networks using the generated dataset to obtain models that generalize to real event-camera scenarios without active-sensor supervision.
impact: Allows practitioners to train high-performing event-based stereo models using widely available image datasets instead of expensive active-sensor annotations, lowering cost and broadening applicability of event-vision methods.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: RGB images → novel view synthesis → proxy events / proxy annotations → training data → event-stereo model

paper_title: EventHub: Data Factory for Generalizable Event-Based Stereo Networks without Active Sensors
paper_authors: Luca Bartolomei, Fabio Tosi, Matteo Poggi, Stefano Mattoccia, Guillermo Gallego
